column1: # Verbs that take a di + noun phrase complement (parlare di, vestire di seta,
# riempire di, fidarsi di). Only these verbs take a di phrase after them in
# the grammar (vp.di-complement); a di phrase after any other verb belongs to
# the noun before it, or is a free time or manner phrase (di notte, di corsa).
# di + infinitive (decidere di partire) is not affected.
# One verb per line as the infinitive without -si/-ne (accorgersi -> accorgere,
# fregarsene -> fregare), then where the evidence comes from:
#   wiktionary-sense    a sense note "[with di ...]" or "(+ di)" in English
#                       Wiktionary (Kaikki.org extract, Italian verbs), not for
#   wiktionary-example  a Wiktionary usage example with the verb + di + noun
#   issue-10            named in the plan of kolov-it/syntango#10
#   tatoeba             a sentence of homograph-set.jsonl attaches a di phrase
#                       to the verb, and the verb selects it there
#                       proposed by a language model (Claude Opus) over the
#                       verbs of verbs.json and common pronominal verbs, with
#                       the example phrase in the third column, and accepted
#                       by a second, independent model (Claude Sonnet) that
